pool.text: Designated capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru and seat of Real Audiencia.
Construction of the Walls of Lima began to protect against pirates.
Strong earthquake severely damaged Lima and destroyed Callao, prompting reconstruction.
José de San Martín reached Lima, granting it heroic title later that year.
Railway line between Lima and Callao completed from Desamparados station.
Iron bridge Puente Balta inaugurated over the Rímac River.
Palace of Pizarro renovated, later serving as presidential residence.
Historic centre building rebuilt after earlier destruction.
Census highlighted major urban problems such as sanitation and housing.
Housing Plan based on Neighborhood Units made official.
Manufacturing accounted for 14% of GNP due to import substitution.
Lima's population reached 1.9 million, showing rapid growth.
Self‑managed community of Villa El Salvador created south of city centre.
Historic Center declared UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Lima generated 53% of Peru's GDP.
Lima Stock Exchange became world's most profitable stock exchange.
El Metropolitano rapid bus system launched across the city.
Lima Metro Line 1 completed after decades of delays.
More than 1.5 million people used Lima's bike lanes.
Bike lanes prevented emission of 526 tons of carbon dioxide.
